chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Ibn Abi Umeyr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the surplus/excess in measuring and weighing, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is not an infringement (exceeding limits), then there is no problem.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to have extra weight or volume in trade measurements according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that minor excesses in measuring and weighing are permissible as long as they do not amount to *ta'addi* (transgression or cheating), a key distinction in Shia commercial jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the principle that fairness in trade is maintained through the absence of deceit rather than requiring absolute mathematical precision in every transaction. It reflects the practical legal approach of the Imams in facilitating daily commerce while preserving ethical integrity.
